## Natural history notes

A tiny introduced big-headed ant characterized by two worker forms: small minor workers and larger-headed major workers with oversized heads for defense and food handling. In Florida, the Navigating Big-headed Ant occurs in disturbed areas as well as mesic or moist woods, nesting in leaf litter, hollow twigs, nuts, and other small cavities, and it is considered a Neotropical introduced species established in the state. Workers forage for tiny insects, seeds, honeydew, nectar, and scavenged material, while also interacting with native leaf-litter ant communities and serving as prey for spiders, beetles, lizards, and other small predators.
